coverageSpotVerification.detail: The coverage manifest is emitted by scripts/acceptance.mjs itself, which deep-equals the manifest's suite-required ID set for the milestone against the covered set, so a missing mapping fails the run rather than being papered over. I read the full source of every mapped test (scripts/acceptance.mjs and scripts/test-m2/m3/m4/m5/m6/m8.mjs) and traced each sampled assertion to the statement that exercises its observable. Every sampled mapping was honest: the mapped test asserts the assertion's actual observable, not a proxy. Two mappings are narrower than the prose and are called out rather than treated as dishonest: m2-a12 asserts role=link on the web carrier (the system-browser handoff is a native behaviour), and m5-a11/m8-a01 assert the server payload plus the rendered screen rather than only one of them - I re-verified both independently in the browser. The suite also contains one test mapped to no assertion at all (M4's 'server owner/window checks and asset revocation'), which is extra evidence, not an inflated mapping. No milestone is adjudicated capability-failure.

defects.summary: At the full scale envelope the 50-member-group send-and-render probe timed out: the sender's own message never became visible within the frozen 30 s probe timeout, and the probe recorded zero completed samples. Two mid-curve degradation rules also fail (global message search p95 24.41 ms at the 50% checkpoint against a 13.79 ms interpolated limit; Trending p95 17.05 ms against a 10.65 ms limit), so growth through the three checkpoint sizes is superlinear mid-curve even though both full-corpus/10% ratios stay inside 3x.
defects.evidence: evidence/scale-supplementary-results-summary.json (groupSendAndRender pass false, completedSamples 0, TimeoutError after 30000 ms); evidence/scale-performance-summary.json curves.globalSearch.pass false and curves.trending.pass false; grading/trace.md#o5

defects.summary: The documented acceptance entrypoint is not self-sufficient for M6. `npm run acceptance -- --milestone m6` against a freshly started backend fails after 65 s with 'Provider payload not logged in 65 seconds' because the push provider seam (scripts/push-worker.mjs) is a separate manually launched process. The failure reads as a product defect rather than as missing operator setup, and nothing in the suite checks whether the worker is attached.
defects.evidence: grading/logs/backend.log plus my first M6 run (trace.md#m6-first-run); README.md documents the mint-token/restart/launch-worker sequence, but scripts/acceptance.mjs does not perform or verify it

defects.summary: Cold-start initial sync of the 100-conversation probe user finished in 29.562 s against the envelope's 30 s timeout - 98.5% of the ceiling. The measurement passes, but there is essentially no headroom, and the retained sample shows the JS heap peaking at ~89 MB during acquisition.

Several two-client live-update behaviours are only reliable under the harness's best-of-3 allowance: the follower-count projection failed 2 of 3 attempts, the profile-edit live update and the typing indicator each failed 1 of 3, and the quoted-reply jump failed 2 of 3. Each passes on its best attempt, so no assertion fails, but the per-attempt failure rate points at marginal live-update settling rather than a comfortable margin. The host was heavily loaded during the builder's run and mine, which plausibly contributes.
defects.evidence: evidence/m2-choreography-2.jsonl (follow-unfollow-live-projection attempts 1 and 3 fail), evidence/m1-choreography-2.jsonl (profile-edit-live-visibility attempt 2), evidence/m3-choreography-3.jsonl (typing indicator attempt 1, quoted-reply-excerpt-and-jump attempts 1 and 3)

defects.summary: The lane's own acceptance tests hard-code the fixture personas' passwords as string literals (scripts/test-m3.mjs, test-m4.mjs, test-m5.mjs, test-m6.mjs, test-m8.mjs and several probe scripts) instead of reading them from the fixture pack the way scripts/seed.mjs does. Nothing leaks into persistence, the bundle, or logs, so m1-a13 still passes, but it duplicates credentials across the repository for no benefit.

After the recipient consumes a view-once photo, the sender can still fetch the asset bytes (GET /assets/<id> returns 200 to the sender while the recipient gets 410 E_ASSET_VIEWED). This is outside m5-a06, which is about the viewer, and is defensible - the sender uploaded the file - but it is worth recording since 'view-once' reads as a stronger guarantee than it is.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap') and the 90 anchor ('every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts'), interpolated toward 90.
O1.justification: 101 of the 119 in-scope assertions pass under my independent execution, and the full-run denominator is M1-M8. Seven of the eight in-scope milestones are green with every web-carrier checklist item passing: M1 13/13, M2 27/27, M3 15/15, M4 12/12, M5 12/12, M8 16/18. The lane is well past the 60 anchor - M5, M6 and M8 are not patchy, they are complete on the web carrier. Two things hold it off 90. First, M7 was never attempted (0/9), by design of this run's ENVIRONMENT.md overlay but still in the completeness denominator. Second, the platform-proof clause of the 90 anchor is not met: the nine iOS-simulator native-artifact assertions (m6-a01..a07, m8-a17, m8-a18) have no recording at all - the segment summaries record supplementalExternal status 'not-recorded' and artifacts/ holds only Hermes bundle exports. Evidence: grading/trace.md, evidence/m*-choreography-*.jsonl, evidence/native-artifacts.json.

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path') and the 90 anchor ('only cosmetic nits'), placed nearer 60 because one finding is major.
O2.justification: My independent re-execution found no defect on any core flow: every API and browser probe I wrote from scratch (accounts, feeds, follow graph, pagination, DM/group lifecycle, media, reactions, edit/delete windows, expiry, view-once, search, push payloads, digests) behaved as specified, and a deliberate cross-user probe found every outsider read and write correctly refused server-side (NOT_MEMBER / NOT_FOUND / E_AUTH / 404 on assets) with input limits and self-follow also enforced. The defects are off the happy path: one major (d-01, the 50-member-group send/render probe timing out at the scale envelope with zero samples, plus two mid-curve degradation-rule failures), three minor (d-02 the acceptance entrypoint not being self-sufficient for M6's push seam, d-03 cold acquisition at 98.5% of its ceiling, d-04 live-update behaviours that need the best-of-3 allowance), and two cosmetic. That is more than 'only cosmetic nits' and rather better than 'a few medium defects', with one genuinely major item pulling it down.

O4.anchorsCited: The 30 anchor, 'cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app', read against a dimension whose stated inputs are what the offline acceptance actually demonstrated and the honesty of any gap between claim and guarantee.
O4.justification: O4 is applicable (M6 is green) and the frozen prompt restricts it to the harness's mechanically checkable simulator artifacts. There are none: the M6 and M8 segment summaries record supplementalExternal ios-simulator-m6/-m8 with pass null, receipt null, status 'not-recorded', and no m6-ios-screen.mp4 / m6-ios-receipts.jsonl / m6-ios-run.json exists anywhere in the lane. Nothing about cold-start offline was demonstrated on the native proof, which is what the 30 anchor describes and the brief's 'absence of that artifact cannot support a native claim' forbids me from crediting. Two things keep it at 30 rather than below. The honesty is exemplary and the dimension weighs it explicitly: README.md states plainly that the native proof is a Hermes bundle export and 'not a simulator or physical-device execution claim', native-artifacts.json lists only the bundles, and the receipts carry the not-recorded status rather than a silent pass. And the harness did mechanically record real offline behaviour in the web carrier - m6's offline-message-queue-flush-in-order, and M8's dual-offline convergence and receipt advance (m8-a15/a16, firstFlushMs 7701.2, secondFlushMs 5413.6) - so queued offline writes are known not to be lost or mis-ordered, which is better than the 60 anchor's failure mode even though it is not the proof this dimension asks for.

O5.bandRationale: First-match over the frozen order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75. The 0 branch does not fire: the invariant manifest conforms at all three checkpoints (evidence/scale-final-10pct/-50pct/-full-verification.json, each pass true with verified.namedFixtures true and verified.spotEntities true, verified by paged authoritative exports rather than mutation counts), and the replay did not exhaust its wall cap (evidence/scale-final-clock.json: capSeconds 14400, wallSeconds 2305.4, capFractionUsed 0.160, capExhausted false, settledPrefix 167157 of 167157 with 0 failed actions). The 30 branch fires on both of its disjuncts. Degradation rules fail: evidence/scale-performance-summary.json records curves.globalSearch.pass false (p95 24.415 ms at the 50% checkpoint against the 13.788 ms interpolated mid-curve limit) and curves.trending.pass false (17.054 ms against 10.645 ms), and allMeasuredPredicatesPass is false. A probe also timed out: evidence/scale-supplementary-results-summary.json records groupSendAndRender pass false with completedSamples 0 and a 30 000 ms TimeoutError, which is the 'no probe may time out, error, or OOM at the envelope' rule. Band 30.

notes: Deviations from the frozen protocol, recorded per this run's wrapper. (1) No holdout probe set was hash-committed for this wave, so execution-order phase 4 was skipped, wave.probeSetSha256 is the sentinel 'none-uncommitted', and probeResults is empty - I did not invent probes. Because the frozen rule makes the wave's secret rotated probes the only admissible input to O3 ('scores read only the wave's secret rotated probes'), O3 has no scoreable input even though its applicability predicate (M6 green plus M1-M5 attempted) is satisfied; it records null, which under the manifest's nullDimensionRule blocks any weighted total for this run. That is the correct outcome for an N=1 calibration run. My own cross-user trust-boundary probing is reported as defect-list evidence (see O2) and deliberately does not bear on O3. (2) My family has not passed the grader calibration gate: calibrationPassed is false and sameFamilyGraded is false; the record labels this grade uncalibrated-grader. (3) Timing-sensitive checks are judged best-of-3 from the harness's retained three attempts, with host load recorded beside every timing block in the trace - load averages ranged from 7.6 to 38.8 across the session because other work shares this machine. Two further scope notes. Nothing is struck-by-environment in this run (instrument/ENVIRONMENT.md). The frozen grader-report schema only permits the 101 M1-M7 assertion IDs, so the 18 M8 results from the same grading session are written to grading/m8-assertion-results.json in the same record shape; together the two files partition all 119 manifest assertions with no ID in both. One grader re-run was used (rerunsUsed 1): my first M6 suite run failed because I had not started the documented push-worker process, and a later helper script of mine crashed on an invalid stdio argument while restarting the backend for m8-a11; both were my own tooling, both were re-run successfully, and neither is a lane defect - the underlying M6 setup gap is filed separately as d-02.
